newsitem.title: UK: French companies to face backdated tax bills - FT.
newsitem.headline: French companies to face backdated tax bills - FT.

text.p: A number of French companies and the French arms of some multinationals are likely to face additional tax bills on profits made last year, the Financial Times reported on Monday.
The French government plans to apply its new 41.6 percent corporate tax rate for financial years ending on January 1, 1997 and onwards, the report said.
The effect is that companies whose financial years straddle two calendar years are set to face a bill for back taxes for the 1996/97 period.
The Financial Times said companies which could be hit included state controlled airline Air France, household appliance group Moulinex and sports equipment manufacturer Salomon.

The three companies have all reported results for the year to end-March 1997. The report said the French government decision meant these figures may have to be adjusted to take account of the higher tax rate.

France's new left-wing government last week announced plans to raise taxes on company profits as part of efforts to lower the budget deficit and help bring the country into line for European monetary union.
